text:
sam: heads-up, ran an NSYS capture on a 4xA100 inference run. timeline shows ~12ms gap where a host memcpy seems to serialize kernels across streams. suspect prefetch->kernel handshake causing latency bump. screenshot: https://internal/trace/2184001111.png

lee: can you paste the nsys command and which commit this started on? :eyes:

sam: nsys profile --sample=cpu --trace=cuda,kern,osrt -o run1.qdrep --target-processes=all python run_infer.py
commit: a1b2c3d4 (batcher heuristic change)

anita: on the timeline the hostToDeviceMemcpyAsync appears after the kernel submit but the copy lane occupies the copy engine and then the kernel stalls waiting for it. Feels like a fallback to blocking hostcopy or pinned pool exhaustion. Are we seeing our pinned buffer allocator fail?

perf-bot: regression alert: p95 latency +9% since a1b2c3d4. Hotspot: kv_cache_prefetch kernel GPU time +30%. Full diff: https://perf/reports/2184001111

lee: upload the CPU swimlanes pls — if CPU scheduling gaps line up with the memcpy calls, prefetch thread preemption could explain the handoff delay.

sam: uploaded NSYS CPU swimlane and perfetto trace here: https://internal/trace/2184001111-cpu.qdrep and https://perfetto/2184001111.pb. The big GPU gap aligns with a ~6ms sched gap on the prefetch thread (THREAD_PREFETCH).

anita: that fits. If the prefetch thread gets preempted while building the staging buffer, the kernel kicks off and then waits on the copy to finish. Two quick experiments: force-use pinned buffers for prefetch, and run with cudaStreamCreateWithPriority to put prefetch on a higher-priority stream.

lee: also investigate kernel selection side — the batcher tweak might prefer a larger GEMM tile that requires extra host staging for KV layout conversion, triggering memcpy on the default copy engine. Can we enable KERNEL_CHOICE logging? set env KERNEL_CHOICE=1 or add lightweight tracepoint around selector.

sam: will run with forced pinned allocation + KERNEL_CHOICE=1 and retake trace. If we see memcpy go async on separate copy engine and gap disappears, we can blame the batcher heuristic tweak and revert.

anita: on A100s copy-engine contention is common. If pinned pool is exhausted the CUDA runtime falls back to pageable copies which serialize. Also try increasing pinned pool or preallocating N buffers during startup to avoid allocations during run. Consider pinning the prefetch CPU thread to an isolated core to reduce preemption risk.

lee: good call. also add a short flamegraph of kernel durations vs memcpy durations next run; that'll make it obvious whether kernel selection changed GPU work makeup.

sam: ack — I'll run two experiment traces: (1) pinned-prealloc + priority stream, (2) revert batcher tweak + baseline. will post results tomorrow. thanks all :thumbsup:
